articles.title: Apple officially restricts employee participation in prediction markets
articles.content: If you're an Apple employee or contractor planning to make money using insider information to gamble in legally-gray "prediction markets," don't. Apple has made its stance clear in a new filing. Don't bother using insider information to gamble in prediction markets Prediction markets skirt the legal definition of gambling, which means they have become widely available in the United States in spite of gambling laws. These markets can be used to bet on everything from when a location might see its first snow to what colors the latest iPhones will be sold in. Regardless of the legality of these markets, Apple has made it clear that using insider information to participate is considered insider trading. While the companies like Polymarket already have insider trading rules, these enable Apple to act against violators from their end. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums
articles.author: Wesley Hilliard <wes@appleinsider.com>
articles.fingerprint: apple employee markets officially participation prediction restricts

articles.title: iPhone Jailbreak Gets Past Lockdown Mode and Survives an Update
articles.content: Just over a week after jailbreaking an iPhone Duo on launch day, hacker team Calif is back with another jailbreak demonstration. This time, the group has jailbroken an iPhone in Lockdown Mode, and the jailbreak appears to persist across an iOS update. Calif shared a video of a jailbroken iPhone 18 Pro with Lockdown Mode on. From there, iOS 27.2 is installed, and the jailbreak remains in place after the update. It isn't clear whether the jailbreak could be installed on a device already running iOS 27.2. Apple describes Lockdown Mode as "extreme protection" for individuals who might be targeted by sophisticated mercenary spyware. Lockdown Mode disables a long list of features, blocking most message attachment types, limiting web technologies, blocking FaceTime calls from unfamiliar callers, disabling invites for Apple services, and removing location information from photos. Lockdown Mode helps, until it doesn't. https://t.co/1UyxPHQUAe — Calif (@calif_io) November 3, 2026 The video shows a malicious PDF sent to the target iPhone using AirDrop to initiate the jailbreak, with the file accepted by the user. Calif hasn't shared additional information, and the exact jailbreak steps are unknown. Earlier this year, Apple told TechCrunch that it was not aware of any successful mercenary spyware attacks against an iPhone in Lockdown Mode. Calif previously said it was disclosing vulnerabilities to Apple and did not plan to release a jailbreak tool for end users. This article, " iPhone Jailbreak Gets Past Lockdown Mode and Survives an Update " first appeared on MacRumors.com Discuss this article in our forums
articles.author: Juli Clover

articles.title: Casio’s cute digital ring watch just got a successor
articles.content: Credit: Casio TL;DR Casio has launched a successor to its original ring watch. The CRW-002 can be set to a 12- or 24-hour format, offers stopwatch functionality, and is water resistant. It will be available this November in silver ($135) and in gold ($155). Casio did something novel in 2024, creating a digital watch in the form of a ring . It later went on to release a second ring watch that incorporated health tracking features. The company is back again with a new ring watch, but this time the device is a direct successor to the original. The design of the CRW-002 is based on the Casio A168 from 1995. It features an injection-molded metal casing and band with a mineral glass face. Under the glass is a seven-segment LCD screen that displays hours, minutes, and seconds. You’ll also find three working side buttons.
articles.author: Ryan McNeal

articles.title: Younger adults will consult AI before a financial advisor on money problems
articles.content: People under 45 are using AI to get financial advice In that cohort, more people (11%) are using AI for financial advice rather than consulting financial advisors (9%) The survey of 2000 UK adults highlights where the financial industry is failing to embrace AI AI has already been a huge disruptor across all industries, but how it is used by consumers has been difficult to predict. Following the use of search to find AI-recommended products, consumers are now consulting AI for financial advice – and using the technology more than they would human financial advisors. A new survey of AI use in financial and monetary tasks has found that 11% under-45s are seeking financial advice from LLM-backed chatbots, more than the 9% who seek guidance from living, breathing advisors with experience in banking and finance products. The research from Attest’s 2027 Consumer trends report highlights some interesting ways in which people expect to be able to use AI, too – including using it to switch to better insurance deals, negotiate disputes, and even cancel unused subscriptions. Money decisions The Attest report reveals numerous interesting insights from its survey of 2000 UK adults. But it is the AI-related revelations that hold particular fascination. While the number of under 45s using AI for financial advice may seem small at 11%, a more significant 41% has admitted they would accept AI-provided financial advice if it was cheaper than equivalent advice from a professional. “For some younger adults, the first conversation about a money decision is already happening with an AI assistant," noted Todd Latham, CEO of Attest. "Financial brands increasingly need to understand the questions people are asking before a customer reaches them, and which providers and products AI puts in front of consumers.” In the world of financial marketing, however, these findings offer a completely different story. Appearing in AI-generated search results is one part of this, but it is the equivalent of an introduction, and doesn’t commit the customer to pursuing any opportunities. AI investment Could people begin to rely on AI to manage investments and find new products within their budgets? At the moment, the answer would seem to be no, as the marketplace isn’t really responding to what AI can do for investments, insurance, and other financial products. Latham confirms this, saying that financial product providers aren’t really communicating with an AI-friendly marketplace. “Our findings across financial products, insurance, travel, tickets and experiences also show how influential that stage can be. Consumers are not only using AI to explore their options,” he explains, “but are increasingly open to letting it take action on their behalf, from cancelling unused subscriptions to switching providers for a better deal. Providers need to understand how their products are represented in these conversations and what gives consumers the confidence to act.” It’s safe to say that if existing providers don’t act quickly, financial products will come from new lenders and brokers who are more suited to AI-based referrals.
articles.author: Christian Cawley

articles.title: North Korean fake job interview led to $6.3B Binance heist
articles.content: North Korean cryptocurrency thieves tricked a Binance software engineer into downloading malware onto their work-issued computer during a fake job interview process before last week's record-breaking $6.3 billion heist . In an incident report published on Tuesday, the cryptocurrency exchange said several techniques - including social engineering via fake job interviews, malware downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint takeover, and an “advanced transaction-authorization method” - led to the October 29 security breach. “Our current investigation indicates that this was a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign,” the incident report said. “It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident.” Over the weekend, the FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation linked to Lazarus Group , known for combining espionage with massive cryptocurrency heists . The Pyongyang-backed crew is also highly adept at job market scams - both posing as IT workers , who are then hired by Western companies , and as potential employers to lure software engineers into downloading malware and infecting corporate devices . With the recent Binance attack, the Norks used the latter. The attack prep began back in June with a supply chain attack when one of its engineers downloaded a malicious Homebrew installation . While the malware was detected by the security team, the device was replaced, and all affected credentials rotated, “Engineer A’s role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker,” the report says. Three months later, the social engineering part of the attack happened. In September, another software engineer was contacted via a “legitimate job-hunting platform” by someone purporting to be a project director who arranged a series of job interviews for the Binance engineer with the fake company. During the first round - a live video interview with the engineer and a fake HR rep - the interviewer “shared a social media account with him, including personal photos and videos posted on the platform, in order to build trust,” according to the report. “This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches.” The second interview with someone purporting to be the CEO of the phony company was conducted on a “popular social chat app,” and toward the end, the CEO instructed the engineer to download an “assignment” containing a malware-laced code repository. The code executed on his work computer during the setup process, which kicked off a series of unauthorized activities. According to Binance, the malware replaced a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version, which executed commands and established communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The attackers also took steps to hide the malicious script and evade detection, and it worked. Binance’s endpoint security tools did not immediately detect the malware. Here’s the script: CREATE /opt/homebrew/Cellar/pyenv/2.8.0/libexec/pyenv_ MODIFY pyenv_ → 3,414 B DELETE .../libexec/pyenv (3,344 B) ← remove the valid pyenv RENAME pyenv_ → pyenv (3,414 B) ← replace it with a malicious version DELETE /opt/homebrew/bin/pyenv (3,414 B) ln (create a new symlink) + spawn zsh Then, on October 20, the miscreants used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain access to the computers of wallet DevOps engineer A and another wallet software developer, Engineer C. Engineer A had a container deployment permission token on his computer, which the Norks soon discovered. On October 29, the attacker accessed Engineer C's computer, used the stolen credentials from Engineer A to deploy a container, and triggered a script to launch the cryptocurrency-stealing attack. As of Tuesday, Binance said it has rebuilt the compromised wallet system and internal AI tool, and replaced all of the affected devices. It also decommissioned all credentials and tokens assigned…

articles.title: Chrome could soon make tab overload a lot easier to manage
articles.content: TL;DR Google Chrome is testing a horizontally scrollable tab bar, making it easier to navigate dozens or hundreds of open tabs. Users can scroll through tabs using their mouse wheel or dedicated arrow buttons, while pinned tabs remain fixed on the left. The feature is currently available in Chrome Canary through an experimental flag, with no confirmed stable release date. Google Chrome is finally learning a trick that rivals like Firefox and Vivaldi have mastered for a few years now. Soon after (finally) giving us vertical tabs to stack all our open webpages neatly along the side, Chrome is learning a thing or two about making its traditional horizontal tab feel a lot more manageable, especially for those who keep several tabs open at once. The tech giant is testing a new horizontally scrollable tab bar, which should make it easier to navigate all open webpages once the tab strip fills up.

articles.title: Bethesda Confirms The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Called 'Sentinel'
articles.content: During a video celebrating Bethesda's 40th anniversary, the studio officially confirmed that The Elder Scrolls VI will be titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. "Thank you for 40 years of shared memories," wrote Bethesda in a separate tweet. "We can't wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it'll be some time before we're ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you." Video Games Chronicle reports: "You know, as we're here in the 40th anniversary, we think about all of the games we've made," Bethesda's executive producer Todd Howard said in the video, walking past a display case. "And you know, every day when I walk by this case, obviously I look at the games and think about them, but more so I think about the teams that made them, and the time and the passion that everybody put into the games. And then what they meant to all of you, and hearing from you, and the time that you spent in them, how meaningful that was to you, and to let you know when we hear that, how meaningful that is to us. And so even though yes, we're looking back, we're also looking forward to all we're doing, particularly with the Fallout franchise and obviously The Elder Scrolls. You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6. And we thought, hey, given the the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called." The video then showed the logo for the game. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Netflix just added AI Discovery as 'test kitchen' for discovering content — here's how to find and use it
articles.content: Netflix announced today (Nov. 3) that the streaming giant is rolling out a new "AI Discover" tab as an experimental way for you to discover new shows and movies. The first version of the new feature will give you recommendations based on your mood. Netflix describes the first experience as "built around themes." You can pick from a range of themes like "Scare Me," "Family Movie Night," or "Quick Watches" that come coupled with a clip from a show or movie. Other somewhat more generic ones include what's trending or based on what you've been watching. (Image credit: Netflix) Selecting a theme brings up recommendations. Or you can choose "Something Different" for a new set of themes. There's also a "Tune Your Recommendations" button that you can use to keep a recommendation or remove the selected show or movie from your recommendations. "Think of AI Discover as our test kitchen: we’re trying out new recipes for discovery, and your use and feedback help us decide which ones to keep, improve, or serve up next. Some may even make their way into the main Netflix experience." Netflix and AI (Image credit: Future / Netflix) This isn't Netflix's first foray into AI. Earlier this year Netflix released a research model , dubbed VOID, that acts like a super version of "Magic Eraser ." It's something you can try right now if you use Hugging Face and you have at least 40GB of VRAM. In 2025, Netflix played around with generative AI-powered ads that were supposed to launch this year. These ads are meant to be more personalized and less disruptive. However, those ads don't appear to have launched yet. Meanwhile, Variety reported in July that more 300 Netflix titles used generative AI this year. Availability Netflix is rolling out the AI Discover tab to English-language Netflix profiles in the United States on supported TVs. The company says it will open up to more people in the coming weeks. If you have it, you should see a red gem with "Discover" in the top menu next to My Netflix. It's not clear how long the rollout will take. I checked on an older Sony Bravia set and a Roku stick on a dumb TV but neither version showed the new tab. Keep an eye out for it. articles.title: Microsoft improves Windows 11 performance on 8 GB PCs as RAM prices keep climbing
articles.content: With RAM getting more expensive, Microsoft is putting more effort into making Windows 11 run better on systems with just 8 GB of memory. Microsoft said on Tuesday that it was "raising the bar for 8 GB Windows 11 PCs," following a renewed focus on memory optimization earlier this year . The changes come as Redmond continues pushing more expensive Copilot+ PCs, which require at least 16 GB of RAM, amid a memory crunch fueled by AI infrastructure demand. Now, Microsoft says a low-end machine with its 8 GB of precious RAM will be up to 20 percent more responsive and 40 percent faster at multitasking thanks to improvements made in memory management. The tweaks are relatively simple, as Microsoft explained, and seem more about adjusting back to the reality that its flagship operating system needs to function on the hardware people can actually afford to purchase if and when they’re forced to upgrade. Windows 11 will now keep up to 2 GB more active data in memory before shunting it to slower storage, as one example. In another instance, Windows will connect directly to Edge when the browser is already running in the background, allowing it to launch up to 33 percent faster, according to Microsoft. Microsoft apps are also being made more efficient, with Teams able to enable Efficiency Mode by default on 8 GB machines, which Microsoft said will make it launch "up to 20 percent faster." Memory efficiency is also being improved by tweaking things like Widgets, which will only load when used instead of always being on, and decreasing the time when Edge tabs go to sleep from two hours to 15 minutes by default. Microsoft said it’s enabling third-party apps to make use of those tweaks, too. Microsoft also included benchmark data in the blog post from a recent bit of research it commissioned. The benchmark report compares a range of 2026 Windows machines with models from 2021, finding that a 2026 Dell XPS 13 with 8 GB of RAM performed about as well as a 2021 Dell XPS 13 with 16 GB across selected workloads. What that means, says Microsoft, is that “the complete PC, not memory capacity alone, shapes the experience.” In other words, please buy some new Windows hardware, even if it’s expensive - we’re begging you. Software optimization can only do so much. “For many people, 8 GB is a great fit for the things they do every day,” Microsoft EVP of Windows and devices Pavan Davuluri wrote in the blog post. “Demanding workloads, such as 3D modeling, advanced video editing, or large-scale data processing benefit from 16 GB of memory or more.” It’s no surprise Microsoft is improving the performance of lower end systems at the same time it’s subtly asking users to buy newer kit, even if it’s just an 8 GB machine - Microsoft may have done well in the past two quarters, but it’s no thanks to Windows devices. Microsoft’s Q4 2026 earnings in late July saw the company rake in cash more broadly, while simultaneously reporting a 7 percent decrease in Windows OEM and devices revenue. Likewise, in its fiscal Q1 2027 results, reported just last week, Microsoft again brought home a mountain of net income, with adjusted earnings reaching $36.4 billion, up 18 percent from the same period last year. Windows OEM and devices revenue, however, was down a whopping 22 percent . It’s hard to think of a reason beyond the fact that hardware prices have shot up with more force than a SpaceX rocket - memory prices are likely to actually make it to Mars, unlike Starship - leaving both consumers and enterprises to stretch those upgrade cycles. If you need to get the most out of that 8 GB Windows 11 PC, you’ll find the latest improvements in 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later. Microsoft is also encouraging users to keep its branded apps up to date, as “some improvements arrive through app updates or through Microsoft Store.” ®
articles.author: Brandon Vigliarolo

articles.title: Apple will now sell you a Mac Studio with 512GB of RAM — but it'll cost you as much as a good-sized family car
articles.content: Apple now sells the M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 512GB of memory from $22,299, rising to as much as $29,799 with a 16TB SSD in tow The $15,500 upgrade costs about 3.9 times more per gigabyte than the same step on the M3 Ultra in 2025, roughly in line with soaring memory prices for PC The entry 512GB build costs less than a base Corolla; only the maxed-out model reaches Camry territory, and orders ship late November to early December Apple has finally delivered the one Mac Studio configuration it left hanging in August. The company's online store now lets buyers configure the M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 512GB of unified memory , right on the schedule it promised. The catch is the price, and it is not a small catch: To unlock the option, you first need the top-tier M5 Ultra with a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU, which starts at $6,799 with 96GB of memory and a 1TB SSD. Selecting 512GB then adds $15,500, for a minimum of $22,299. A memory crisis meets top-of-the-line hardware To even get to the pricing stated above, you first need the top-tier M5 Ultra with a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU, which starts at $6,799 and includes 96GB of memory and a 1TB SSD. Selecting 512GB then adds $15,500, for a minimum of $22,299. Max out the storage at 16TB and the bill reaches $29,799. Orders placed today are quoted for delivery between late November and early December 2026, so you are in for a bit of a wait even if you are willing to shell out that kind of money. When Apple unveiled the new Mac Studio , it called the 512GB ceiling "staggering." That adjective, as it turns out, applies to the price just as much as the capacity. At $22,299, the cheapest 512GB Mac Studio barely undercuts a base 2026 Toyota Corolla LE , which carries a $23,125 MSRP. Spec the SSD all the way to 16TB, however, and the comparison becomes literal. A 2026 Toyota Camry , Toyota's midsize family sedan, lists for just under $30,000 before destination fees, and the Mac Studio, when maxed out, clocks in at exactly the same ballpark. Another way to look at it: the memory upgrade alone costs nearly three times as much as the $5,499 entry-level M5 Ultra Mac Studio. None of this would sting quite as much had Apple not sold the same capacity for a fraction of the price last year. When the M3 Ultra Mac Studio launched in March 2025, upgrading from 96GB to 512GB cost $4,000, and a 512GB build with 1TB of storage cost $9,499 . Today's equivalent costs a whopping $12,800 more. In March 2026, after the memory shortage hit hard, Apple quietly pulled the 512GB option from the M3 Ultra and raised the price of the 256GB upgrade from $1,600 to $2,000 . By May, the 256GB tier had also gone , leaving the M3 Ultra on sale with only 96 GB. In late June, Apple raised prices across most of its Mac and iPad lineup, with the M3 Ultra Mac Studio jumping $1,300 to $5,299 . "We have never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly," the company said at the time . Doing the math, that 416GB step from 96GB to 512GB cost about $9.62 per gigabyte on the M3 Ultra. On the M5 Ultra, it works out to about $37.26 per gigabyte, roughly 3.9 times as much, indicating that a near fourfold cost increase is now being passed on to Apple's most deep-pocketed consumers. That multiple is less outrageous than it first appears. In April 2026, Tim Cook warned of " significantly higher memory costs " from the June quarter. In June, he told The Wall Street Journal that Apple needed memory pricing and supply "to return to reasonable levels for consumer products." On the July earnings call, his last as CEO before John Ternus took over, he described the market as "a hundred-year flood on the memory pricing." IDC figures cited in a recent iThinkDiff earnings preview put memory costs up roughly 350% year on year. If that holds for the high-capacity memory an Ultra needs, Apple's per-gigabyte increase is roughly in line with the market rather than far above it. The shape of the price curve is harder to wave away for Apple.…

articles.title: iPadOS 27.3 Expands Siri Mode to Camera App
articles.content: iOS 27 added a Siri tab to the Camera app on the iPhone 15 Pro and newer for convenient access to Visual Intelligence. Starting with iPadOS 27.3, which is in beta starting today , that feature has expanded to iPad Pro and iPad Air models with the M1 chip and newer, as well as the iPad mini models with the A17 Pro and A20 Pro chips. When you switch to Siri mode in the Camera app on supported iPhone or iPad models, you can get information about things around you. On the iPad, the feature works with the Apple Pencil, meaning you can take a photo and then circle an object with the Apple Pencil and use Visual Intelligence to receive information about the object. Visual Intelligence was already available on the iPad, so the addition of a Siri tab in the Camera app mainly provides a new way of accessing it. iPadOS 27.3 is expected to be released in December. articles.title: Firefox's New Mini Window Is Every Multitasker's Dream
articles.content: Mozilla is testing a new Firefox Nightly feature called Mini Window that lets users pop an entire webpage into a small, always-on-top window stripped of most browser controls. "The idea behind the Firefox Mini Window feature is simple: allow users to move a currently open tab (or a section of a tab) into a separate mini window," writes ZDNet's Jack Wallen. "Think of it as moving a tab from one window to what appears like a web app." From the report: At first blush, there's no address bar, controls, scroll bar, or anything else that would normally be associated with Firefox. The Mini Window appears to be a web app, without having to actually create it. However, when I hover my cursor inside the Mini Window, I do see the address bar, the back/forward/reload buttons, and the window close button -- and that's it. The browser gets out of your way, so the only thing I see is the content. On top of that (pun intended), the Mini Window stays on top of other Firefox windows, so I can have that popped-out content always in focus while I work on other things. This feature comes in handy when I'm working with limited display space (say, on a laptop) and need to reference a page while working on another. For multitasking, it comes in very handy. [...] Let's say I'm writing a paper on Linux and need to read a particular article for background information. I could have my document open in the main window, and then open the article in question in a Mini Window. I could then reference the article without having to click back and forth between them -- even when working on a smaller display. Here's another use case I've found: When using MacOS's Stage Manager feature, I only have one window available at a time. The Mini Window bypasses that limitation, so I can have my main browser window focused as well as the page open in the Mini Window. Another handy way I like to use Mini Window is to open a favorite search engine, move it to a Mini Window, and then I have an always-ready search tool at my fingertips. I could also open my favorite AI service and use it in the same way. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Those Jeff Bezos hair transplant photos are very fake
articles.content: These edits of Jason Statham (left) and Jeff Bezos are a bit jarring, but that’s sort of the point. | Image: The Verge Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor Jason Statham have a distinctive feature in common: They're both famously bald, and that definitely hasn't changed in the last few days. However, there are some images of the two men circulating around X , Threads , and Bluesky in which they both have substantially more hair than their usual shaved look, which in Bezos' case appears to be very freshly transplanted. It's all just photo editing fakery, AI or otherwise. articles.title: Safari finally gets vertical tabs — and a new way to make any site dark, all thanks to OS 27.3
articles.content: Safari is getting some useful updates Vertical tabs will arrive for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, but it's only in the dev betas for now Other features like Adaptive Dark Mode and Siri AI browser tools are coming, too, along with our first glimpse of the new Audio Intelligence capabilities On the global web browser stage, Safari lags behind Chrome, but when it comes to Apple's 2.5 billion customers, it reigns supreme. Yet, even those devoted users might've noticed that their favorite browser was lacking at least one long-sought feature. Now, with the introduction of Dev Betas for iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3, they're getting their wish. In beta today, the platform upgrade actually brings a series of relatively small but important updates to Safari across the iPhone Duo, iPad, and Mac, but chief among them is vertical tabs. As is often the case, Apple didn't invent this idea. I started using vertical tabs in, of all things, Microsoft Edge years ago, and even Chrome recently added them. Now, with the Safari update, you can open the Safari View Menu or hop into Settings and select vertical tabs. Future Future By default, the tabs, which will live on the left side of your browser window in iPadOS and macOS (and iOS for the iPhone Duo), appear as icons — a space-saving measure. You can hover over any of them for a quick look at the hidden browser window. There are other vertical tab features like the ability to pin tabs at the top of your list by dragging and dropping them, and tab groups. The tabs will work on the iPad and, yes, the new iPhone Duo in portrait and landscape mode. (Image credit: Future) The platform updates also bring a new kind of Dark Mode. Instead of only showing the mode on web pages that support it, Safari will offer to tune unsupported pages to Dark Mode too, but in a way, Apple promises, that won't ruin the sites. The Adaptive Dark Mode will automatically darken light backgrounds, invert logos and graphics, recolor vector artwork, lift raised surfaces, and even detect shadows and adjust them. It will not touch already darkened sites. For developers, there are new tags they can use that will prevent Adaptive Dark Mode from adjusting them. The update is also bringing some Siri AI browser tools to Safari for hardware that supports Apple Intelligence. Siri AI already has, with your permission, an awareness of what's on your screen, but with this update, it'll see entire web pages (beyond what you see in the screen frame) and even hidden tabs. This can be useful when you want to do wholesale organization and group tabs. Say you want all tabs relating to a trip to Malta sorted by activity, or you need all your car shopping tabs grouped and organized by car price. Siri AI can, with new Custom Actions, do your bidding on the browser and clean up your history by topic, site, and time period. It might be useful when you don't want someone seeing that you've been shopping for the last few days on a particular site for that coveted gift. There might be other reasons for targeted history scrubbing, but no need to get into that here. (Image credit: Apple) Other notable updates arriving in iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3 Dev Beta 1 include: Siri App Actions will let Siri AI dig even more deeply into your system by organizing files, making trip plans, creating playlists, scheduling group messages, and finding the best photos to share. The promised Apple Health app overhaul , which uses Apple Intelligence, will give you more insights from your health data. The pair of Audio Intelligence features that will work with your Apple Watch Series 12: Live rewind, for recalling what was said in conversation (you have to double-press the watch crown to read the last snippet of conversation). It might be a great tool for settling he said/he said arguments. Siri Recap, which, when enabled, can use Apple Intelligence to recap and summarize an entire talk, speech, lesson, or maybe a TED Talk. The changes are coming to…

articles.title: Nvidia is happy to take your money whether you're using open or closed models, says Jensen Huang
articles.content: Nvidia doesn't seem to care whether open or closed models win out as long as its hardware is powering the infrastructure. "We love closed models," CEO Jensen Huang said. "There's a solid place in the world for closed frontier models. But the world has so many good ideas … The idea that all of us would be based on general intelligence is not logical." Speaking with Lin Qiao, CEO and founder of Fireworks.ai , at the company's Forge event in San Francisco on Tuesday, Huang wasn't ready to throw Nvidia's cloud customers, which help deliver the proprietary AI of Anthropic and OpenAI, under the onrushing open model bus. But having come to the defense of open weight models in July to push back against protectionist pressure from the leadership of Anthropic and OpenAI, Huang recognizes the economic and strategic appeal of AI services that are more affordable and less locked-in. Most of the value in the world, he said, is captured in specialized intelligence, which is to say AI models trained on specific domains of knowledge. "The opportunity for artificial superintelligence is already here," he said. "By taking an open frontier model, adapting it, and providing it with your domain knowledge, your access to your specialized tools, and the proper evaluation, you should be able to create essentially a superintelligence." That aligns with Fireworks' business – offering a platform for companies to train and run models tuned to their specific needs. Coincidentally, that platform just received an infusion of 25,000 Nvidia GPUs to support its expansion in Europe . Huang's endorsement of open models also fits with Qiao's introductory remarks about the need for the AI frontier to be open. But he largely avoided echoing Qiao's focus on the cost savings allowed by working with open models. In her introductory remarks, Qiao stood on stage backlit by a slide composed of ten headlines highlighting the extraordinary cost of unchecked token spending. "Cost is out of control," she said. "Business cannot scale without borrowing a lot of money." That theme was echoed in a subsequent session helmed by Kay Zhu, co-founder and CTO of AI workspace Genspark, titled Gen-1 Slides: Frontier Quality Without Frontier Costs. Gen-1 Slides, Genspark's model for generating slide decks, was built atop MiniMax M3 and tuned to deliver results comparable to Anthropic's Opus 5 at 1/17th the cost – $0.30/M tokens compared to $5/M. Asked what might become commonplace next year but seems unlikely today, Huang said this year's breakthrough has been agent harnesses that turn AI models into agents. He added, "I would say the big breakthrough we'll talk about next year, maybe this is a little self-serving, is how Open Shell has enabled every company in the world to deploy agents safely, confidently." Given the nod to make a second prediction, Huang added, "I would say that the second big breakthrough for industry would be hardware in the loop. And hardware in the loop basically is robotic systems." Given Nvidia's evident interest and investment in robotics , that would be fortuitous. ®

articles.title: Ukraine’s drone strikes spur hasty Russian plans for underground data centers
articles.content: Russian tech companies are scrambling to harden and hide their data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged facilities housing AI supercomputers and disrupted cloud services for millions of Russian users. Meanwhile, the Kremlin is requiring data center owners to reserve computing capacity for emergency state needs and has even authorized possible use of foreign data centers. These consequences of Russia's war against Ukraine come as the Russian military has bombarded Ukrainian cities with drones and missiles nearly night and day in recent months, along with specifically targeting Ukrainian data centers since late September. But Ukraine has retaliated with its own drone strikes on military and infrastructure targets across Russia, degrading or knocking out data centers operated by Russian tech giant Yandex , the state-owned bank Sberbank, social media site VKontakte, and the Russian Ministry of Finance. Now, state-owned telecommunications company Rostelcom has raised the possibility of moving some Russian data centers underground in talks with the nickel and palladium mining company Norilsk, according to Russian newspaper Vedomosti . The industry publication Data Center Dynamics also pointed to a recent proposal by a Russian regional governor to build data centers within open-pit coal mines while planting green public parks above as camouflage. articles.title: DuckDuckGo fires back at Google: Schools don't need AI to search the web
articles.content: Google says it's giving schools more control over AI, but there's a meaningful catch that parents can't ignore. Schools that want to keep AI out of the classroom will also have to give up Google Search through student accounts. In a Tuesday announcement , Google said it will disable access to several products, including Gemini and Google Search, for K–12 student accounts unless school administrators turn them on. But there's one thing schools won't be able to do: Keep Google Search while blocking its built-in AI features. "If a school is not comfortable with that and simply wants AI off, then they have the choice to not have Search on at all," Chris Phillips, Google's vice president of education, told Chalkbeat . The changes, expected to roll out in early 2027, could leave school districts choosing between allowing AI-generated answers in Search or finding another way for students to research their homework. Why Google Search is part of the deal (Image credit: Getty Images) Google has spent years integrating AI into its search engine, most visibly through AI Overviews, which provide generated summaries above traditional search results. Now, those features are becoming a sticking point for schools that want students to research independently without relying on AI-generated answers. "Search and AI are deeply integrated," Chris Phillips, Google's vice president for education, told The New York Times . According to Phillips, students in schools that prohibit AI entirely will not have access to Google Search through their school accounts. Instead, they'll see a message indicating that the service is unavailable. The restriction applies to school-managed accounts under the new controls, Google has also made it clear that administrators can enable individual products, including Gemini and Google Search, rather than accepting every AI service as a package. But the problem is much greater because schools still cannot offer an entirely AI-free version of Google Search. DuckDuckGo says schools don't have to choose Not everyone agrees with Google's explanation for keeping AI in Search. In a statement to Tom's Guide, DuckDuckGo pushed back on the idea that schools must accept AI-generated answers to keep using a search engine. "There is no technical reason why Google can't turn AI off," the company said, arguing that AI Overviews is a search feature similar to maps, flights or weather that Google can choose when to display. DuckDuckGo points to its own search engine as an alternative. Unlike Google, it allows users to adjust how often AI-generated answers appear or turn them off completely. The company also offers noai.duckduckgo.com , a version of its search engine that automatically disables AI features and filters AI-generated images from results without requiring users to change any settings. Schools looking to avoid Google's restrictions can also make DuckDuckGo their default search engine , according to the company. Google is also bringing AI tutoring to Search (Image credit: Shutterstock) Alongside the changes to school controls, Google is expanding Guided Learning, an AI-powered feature designed to help students understand subjects rather than simply giving them answers. Guided Learning is already available in Gemini, and Google announced that the feature is now available globally in Google Classroom. The company is also bringing similar capabilities to Google Search, beginning with a pilot in selected U.S. schools later this month. For example, a student who searches for help with a physics problem might receive questions and explanations that guide them through the solution rather than an immediate final answer. Someone researching a book report could receive prompts encouraging them to think through the material. Google calls this approach "productive struggle," the idea that students learn more when they work through challenges rather than immediately receiving solutions. articles.title: iOS 27.3 Adding New StandBy Mode Features to iPhone 11 and Newer
articles.content: iOS 27.3 will expand new StandBy features first introduced on the iPhone Duo to all iPhone models compatible with the update, according to Apple. StandBy mode makes it easier to view information at a glance while your iPhone is placed on a charger and in a landscape position. It effectively turns an iPhone into a bedside clock with some extra details. On the iPhone Duo, StandBy also works when the device is folded like a book or a tent, even when it is not charging. The new StandBy features coming to the iPhone 11 and newer: Updated versions of the Analog and Digital Clock faces with more options to customize the color and complications on them An updated Photos face that lets users pick Shared Albums New faces, including Calendar and Weather The ability to create multiple versions of each type of face and swipe between them iOS 27.3 also introduces vertical tabs in Safari , reintroduces Apple's redesigned Health app , enables some Apple Intelligence features in China , and more. The first iOS 27.3 developer beta was released earlier today, and Apple said the update will be released to the public in December. articles.title: NVIDIA Shows 3 Ways to Speed Up MoE Inference on DGX Spark, Lifting Ling-3.0-flash Throughput 42.5%
articles.content: NVIDIA’s latest technical blog shows how to speed up mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference on one DGX Spark . The test model is Ant Group inclusionAI’s Ling-3.0-flash , a 124B-parameter MoE with 5.1B active parameters. NVIDIA stacked three optimizations: a new MoE kernel backend, an FP8 output layer and built-in speculative decoding. On all 1,319 GSM8K questions, decode throughput rose 42.5% with no statistically detectable accuracy change. So why is it relevant for Devs? DGX Spark is a desktop system, not a data center node. NVIDIA’s results show a 124B MoE serving single-user requests faster on that desk-side box. The technical post also shows where MoE decode time goes, and how to cut it. TL;DR Size: Ling-3.0-flash-fp4: 124B total, 5.1B active per token; 256K native context. Runs on: One NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, 128 GB unified memory, 273 GB/s), batch size one. Performance: Three stacked optimizations lift GSM8K decode throughput from 37.81 to 53.89 tokens/s. Best: +42.5% throughput and -24.5% mean latency, with accuracy flat (96.89% vs 96.82%). Lagging: Synthetic gains (+185.1%) shrink on GSM8K as MTP acceptance drops from 3.90 to 2.68. Why is MoE decoding on DGX Spark memory-bound? DGX Spark is NVIDIA’s desktop system built on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip. It offers 128 GB of unified memory and 273 GB/s of memory bandwidth. Peak compute is up to 1 petaFLOP of sparse FP4. NVIDIA rates it for inference on models up to 200B parameters. In the NVIDIA technical post , the NVIDIA team profiled Ling-3.0-flash-fp4 at batch size 1. Decoding was memory-bound: reading model weights drove execution time. Two operations stood out, the MoE computation and the LM head that scores the vocabulary. That points to two levers: move fewer bytes per decode step, and generate more tokens per verification round. The baseline followed the official W4A8 recipe. It used FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernels, CUTLASS dense GEMM and an FP32 LM-head path. On a synthetic 32K-input, 2K-output test, it ran at 27.71 ms per token (36.09 tokens per second). What are the 3 optimizations? 1. Humming MXFP4 MoE kernels: NVIDIA swapped FlashInfer’s MoE backend for Humming , an independent kernel library. Humming uses NVRTC to compile kernels at runtime for the actual matrix shapes, data types and GPU. That includes the narrow 768-wide expert layer. Each kernel compiles in seconds. The FlashInfer CUTLASS path compiles 97 targets with ninja, on the order of tens of minutes. Throughput rose 9.3% to 39.45 tokens per second. 2. Online FP8 LM head: The LM head is a 157,184 x 2,560 matrix stored in BF16. Every generated token reads all of it. Quantizing only this layer to FP8 at load time halves those reads. Setting SGLANG_ENABLE_FP8_LM_HEAD=1 enables it. It cannot be combined with the baseline –enable-fp32-lm-head option. Combined with Humming, throughput reached 43.94 tokens per second. That is 21.7% over baseline and 11.4% over Humming alone. 3. MTP speculative decoding with NEXTN: Ling-3.0-flash ships with a built-in NEXTN prediction layer, so no extra draft model is needed. It drafts three tokens, and the model verifies four positions at once. Verification costs about 2.26x a normal decode step. The main cost is MoE, not attention. Verifying four tokens can activate up to 32 experts instead of 8. On the synthetic test, an average of 3.90 tokens were accepted per round. Throughput jumped to 102.88 tokens per second, up 185.1%. The three techniques do not overlap. Humming and the FP8 LM head cut the cost of each step. MTP cuts the number of steps. The integration trap: Stacking these is not automatic. With FP8 LM head and MTP both on, the draft must share the full LM-head module. Otherwise the framework silently falls back, and the draft interprets FP8 weights as BF16. Accept length drops to 1.00, and throughput falls below the unoptimized baseline. The NVIDIA team advises checking at startup that each optimization is active. NVIDIA points to the Ling cookbook…

articles.title: Amazon rewrites its software engineering playbook for an era when AI writes the code
articles.content: Marc Brooker, an AWS VP and distinguished engineer, leads Velocity Labs, a small team inside Amazon’s cloud unit. (Amazon Photo) Last month, a small team inside Amazon Web Services called Velocity Labs went from concept to the public release of a new open-source AI model in less than a week. The group, whose existence hasn’t been previously reported, was formed in April. Velocity Labs has about 35 people, most of them in Seattle. The idea is to think beyond Amazon’s normal product-oriented approach, building quick prototypes in areas of AI that the company sees as underexplored and increasingly important to customers. “We have noticed how the open-source community, and some of our competitors, experiment with new ideas, and deliver initial products fast,” the company says in job listings . “With Velocity Labs we are building an organization that can move faster, explore more, and make sure AWS is at the cutting edge of innovation in agentic AI.” Inside the group, scientists and engineers work together, and they’re encouraged to cross over: engineers engage in research, and scientists do engineering work. Velocity Labs is an example of the ways Amazon is trying “to create organizations that we think are going to be better suited to working with this new set of tools,” said Marc Brooker, an AWS vice president and distinguished engineer who leads the team. For the vast majority of Amazon’s developers, he said, AI agents now write almost all the code that would have previously been written by hand. Redefining the role: The team is part of Amazon’s larger rethinking of software development for the AI era, laid out in revised guidelines that the company’s engineering leaders sent to its developers earlier this year. A letter that accompanied the guidelines, published last week under the byline of Michael “Terk” Terkowitz, a VP and distinguished engineer in Amazon’s stores business, advises engineers to learn AI now and to stay close to their customers and products. The letter acknowledges that as Amazon has grown, some engineers and managers have become “less connected to their customers and business.” Amazon has never published its underlying role guidelines for software engineers, and it declined to provide a copy of the revised version for this article. Brooker, one of the authors of the accompanying letter, said in an interview that the update emphasizes measuring engineers and teams by outcomes rather than inputs. “We had seen these anti-patterns in the industry of folks really focusing on how many tokens are you spending, how many lines of code are you committing,” Brooker said, explaining that those kinds of measures don’t equate to customer value. Asked whether AI use is part of performance reviews or promotions, Brooker said, “Not directly in a metrics sense.” It could factor in, he said, to the extent that it makes someone a stronger performer. The letter doesn’t dismiss usage metrics entirely. Amazon has found that they “correlate well with the outputs that matter” and expects that to continue “for some time,” it says. But what’s important, the letter says, is to use them “with care and judgement.” Amazon engineers have described pressure to use AI tools. Three developers told The New York Times last year that managers were pushing them to use AI, raising output goals and becoming less forgiving about deadlines, with some coders saying their jobs had begun to resemble warehouse work. Amazon has set a goal for more than 80% of its developers to use AI each week, the Financial Times reported . In May, Amazon shut down an internal leaderboard called KiroRank — which ranked employees by how much they used Kiro , the company’s AI coding tool — after finding that some were using the tool excessively just to climb the rankings, the FT reported. Asked whether that episode was part of the impetus for the revised guidelines, Brooker said he didn’t recall the leaderboard or the details surrounding it.…

articles.title: These muscle-reading wearables let you use voice input without speaking a word
articles.content: TL;DR Subvocal’s glasses tech uses radar to analyze the movement of muscles in your mouth. From those readings, it can extrapolate the words you’re saying — even if you’re just silently mouthing them. Pre-orders for the wearable are open now, with orders expected to ship in Q1 2027. Ever since mobile devices started getting smaller than a laptop, engineers have been tackling the difficult question of how we’re supposed to enter text. We’ve gone from tiny physical keyboards , to touchscreen keyboards, to gesture-based glide typing . On wearables, the situation’s even trickier, and it can feel like we’re stuck either using voice input or left awkwardly poking in the air at a virtual keyboard. But now one startup has a clever, hands-free solution that works silently. How many of you speak aloud to yourself as you type? Or maybe when proofreading, do you ever silently mouth the words as you’re reading them? You might be a prime candidate for trying out Subvocal’s glasses tech, which translates silent mouth movements into written text (via Hacker News ).

articles.title: Smugglers are reportedly soldering top-tier HBM onto deliberately useless processors to sneak it into China, and the trick isn't new
articles.content: Smugglers are reportedly pairing Samsung and SK hynix HBM with deliberately useless processors so the package passes export regulations as a low-end chip Shenzhen workshops then heat the packages, pry off the HBM3E, and sell it for about $4,000 a stack, mostly to Huawei customers The trick exploits a December 2024 BIS exclusion for co-packaged chips, but only "where the dominant function" is processing Some of the most sought-after memory in the AI industry is reportedly reaching China attached to processors that were designed never to be used. A new report from The Information claims smugglers are taking high-bandwidth memory (HBM) made by Samsung and SK hynix, packaging it alongside cheap, low-performance server chips, and exporting the combination as an ordinary processor with a CPU that nobody really wants. Once the packages reach mainland China, workshops heat them until the solder gives way, pry off the memory stacks, and discard the processors. A processor nobody wants paired to memory that has Chinese buyers lining up for more The scheme reached a much wider audience when Chinese tech commentator AB Kuai.Dong summarized the report for his followers on X , describing the decoy chips as "clunky" processors and calling the arrangement a "compliant export. Reporting from Wccftech sheds more light on the smuggler at the center of the story: a man in his 40s, fluent in Chinese and Korean, with a background in the Korean chip industry. He runs what is on paper an ordinary chip design firm with an interesting caveat: Its processors are reportedly so weak that no data center would buy them, which is the point: they give the company a reason to order top-tier HBM in volume. Packaging houses in Taiwan, South Korea and Southeast Asia then reportedly bond the memory and the processor onto a single substrate, and the package ships to Hong Kong declared for export reasons as a processor. From there, it crosses into the mainland in luggage, car trunks, and the bags of daily cross-border commuters, being smuggled en masse to Chinese workshops. The last step is arguably the riskiest: Seoul Economic Daily reports that excessive or overly rapid heat can warp or crack the memory stacks, and that failure rates are high. The margins are large enough that nobody involved minds the potential risk. Skirting export compliance at $4,000 a stack The entire process is possible due to a gap that sits in the rules the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) published in December 2024 . Those rules require a license to ship standalone HBM with a bandwidth density above 2GB/s/mm^2 to China, but a technical note excludes co-packaged chips that combine HBM and logic. Those are instead judged by the package's processing performance. Pair a fast memory stack with a slow processor, and you get a chip cleared for export even if the primary goal is to secure the HBM rather than the underlying chip. To its credit, the BIS did anticipate this in some form: The same note keeps HBM under control when it is permanently affixed to a logic die that merely serves as a control interface to the physical layer, so a memory stack sitting on a thin controller does not escape. What it did not account for was a processor engineered to be useless. Interestingly, the exclusion applies, in the regulator's own words, only "where the dominant function of the co-packaged integrated circuit is processing." It is hard to argue that processing is the dominant function of a package whose value lies almost entirely in its memory. Nothing about this approach is new: In April 2025, SemiAnalysis reported that CoAsia Electronics, Samsung's HBM distributor in Greater China, was shipping HBM2E to Taiwanese design services firm Faraday Technology, which had SPIL package it with a low-cost 16nm logic die before sending it on to China, where the memory could reportedly be desoldered. "The HBM export ban is specifically for raw HBM packages," the analysts wrote. Faraday…

articles.content: Apple is planning an Apple Watch Activity Challenge for Veterans Day, which takes place next Wednesday in the United States. Apple Watch owners who complete the challenge will win an Apple Watch activity award in the Fitness app. Earn this award on November 11 by doing any workout for 11 minutes or more. Like all of Apple's Activity Challenges, the Veterans Day challenge will reward users with animated stickers that can be used in the Messages app. Apple does a Veterans Day Activity Challenge each year, and also often offers Veterans Day-themed content in the App Store , Apple TV app, Books app, and more. articles.title: Soniox STT v6 Adds Agent Text Input and Echo Filtering for Voice Agents
articles.content: Soniox has released Soniox STT v6 , the latest generation of its speech-to-text API. Soniox STT v6 is a speech-to-text model that reads what a voice agent says while hearing the caller. It uses that text to recognize short replies and to drop the agent’s own voice. The release ships as stt-rt-v6 for streaming and stt-async-v6 for files , across 60+ languages. TL;DR Size: Soniox STT v6 is a proprietary hosted model, no parameter count published. Runs on: Soniox cloud API only (WebSocket streaming and async REST). No self-hosted or on-device option disclosed. Performance: Soniox calls it “significantly” more accurate than v5, but publishes no v6 numbers yet. Best: Price. $0.12/hour streaming and $0.10/hour async, with diarization and language ID bundled. Worst: Zero independent v6 results. Its v5 predecessor scored 1.34% semantic WER on Pipecat, behind v4’s 1.25%. What problem does Soniox STT v6 solve? In a cascaded voice agent, STT usually hears only the caller. It never sees the question being answered. Short answers suffer most. In Soniox’s docs , “River Roast” becomes “River Road” and “a tow” becomes “a tour.” The second problem is echo. Agent audio leaks back through speakerphones and laptops, gets transcribed as user speech, and the agent interrupts itself. How does agent text input work? You enable it with one flag in the start request: "enable_agent_text_input": true . It is only available on stt-rt-v6 , not the async model. While the agent speaks, you stream its words on the same WebSocket as the caller’s audio. Each message is a small JSON frame: {"type": "agent_text", "text": "...", "end_of_segment": true} . Timing matters. Messages carry no timestamps, so the model places text where it arrives in the audio stream. Soniox recommends sending each piece 500 ms to 1 second before playback, paced by TTS timestamps. On barge-in, you flush what was already played, send end_of_segment: true , and drop the unplayed rest. The agent’s text never appears in the returned transcript. How does agent voice echo cancellation work? With agent text input on, v6 knows what the agent is saying. It uses that to separate leftover agent audio from caller speech and filter it out. It keeps listening during playback, so callers can still interrupt. It does not replace acoustic echo cancellation. It handles what your existing AEC leaves behind , so keep AEC on. What else changed in v6? Better voice typing: numbers, currencies, units, dates, IDs, names and specialized terms. Spoken commands like “period” or “new line” are written as words, so your app applies them. Improved meeting transcription and speaker diarization, live or recorded. Stronger accents, code-switching and language switching within a sentence. There is one formatting change to test before upgrading. v6 writes “15 dollars and 20 cents” as spoken, not “$15.20”. Hyphens in codes appear only when spoken. How does Soniox compare on benchmarks? Soniox has not published v6 accuracy or latency numbers. Its benchmarks page still reports v5 on the open-source Pipecat STT benchmark . It uses 1,000 real-world samples and measures semantic WER plus time to final segment (TTFS). On it, stt-rt-v5 scores 1.34% semantic WER, 83.3% perfect transcripts and 260 ms median TTFS. Its P95 latency is 305 ms. Azure posts the lowest WER mean at 1.21%, but at 1,016 ms median latency. articles.content: OpenAI's hardware team used GPT-6 Astra to design a device for the Codex coding agent in under a week, handling everything from the enclosure to the circuit board to the firmware. Several revision rounds were needed before production because the model didn't always account for manufacturing tolerances. A newer internal model scores significantly higher on OpenAI's engineering benchmark, though the company isn't sharing details. articles.content: Revolut says that in less than a year it's managed to slash its AI coding inference costs by roughly 90 percent by making self-hosted models its default instead of relying primarily on commercial services like Claude. Speaking at the AI Engineer conference in New York last month, David Abitbol, ops and infrastructure lead at the British fintech, described how it saw a 60 percent improvement in coding time and a 70 percent improvement in lead time following its rollout of AI coding tools to roughly 2,000 engineers. Revolut initially adopted GLM-5.1 before moving to GLM-5.3, which it now serves using 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs. Prior to its switch to GLM, Revolut had been experimenting with AI, deploying Gemini in early 2025 and Claude Code in early 2026. "We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI. We were seeing engineers spend $1,000 a month, $10,000 a month with not so much ROI, and so when we launched it we launched it with strict budget limits," Abitbol said. Because of this, engineers only had access to a limited number of tokens, so the company began investigating self-hosting its own models. At $0.30 per million input/output tokens, self hosting GLM 5.1 cost about a tenth of using OpenAI's Codex or Anthropic's Claude Code. And, as it turned out, when tokens are cheap, you stop worrying about how many they use or what they use them for. While Revolut did see improvements to coding speed, Abitbol noted the biggest bottleneck wasn't actually the code. Instead, he says the biggest gains came from letting the AI models deal with things like debugging and Jira and Confluence tickets. "When you have unlimited tokens, you're free to do that," he said. "You no longer have to save your tokens for the end of the quarter or the most difficult task." Developed by Chinese open weights model dev Z.ai, GLM 5.1 isn't exactly a small model. At roughly 754 billion total parameters (40 billion activated for each token generated), the model requires roughly 380 GB of GPU memory just to hold the weights and another 6-26 GB per user to maintain context depending on precision. To serve GLM-5.3 at scale, Revolut deployed 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, equivalent in GPU count to seven eight-GPU DGX B200 systems. But as Abitbol noted, the greatest performance gains didn't come from adding GPUs, but rather tuning the model's hyperparameters along with switching to NVFP4 quantization, implementing disaggregated prefill and decode, and tuning context lengths. One key takeaway was that supporting a one-million-token context window doesn't necessarily make such a large window useful or efficient. "Long context is a scam. You really need to be mindful of that," Abitbol said. "Even though you can serve one million tokens, 256 [thousand] is really what you need." With these optimizations, Abitbol says that the company was able to achieve sub 3-second time to first token on context windows of around 256,000 tokens, and generation speeds of around 200 tokens a second, both of which he notes are the sweet spot for the company's software engineers. "What you want to aim for is a sub-3 second time to first token. This is empirical evidence. As soon as you exceed 5 seconds, my Slack inbox starts to blow up," Abitbol said. "In terms of throughput, it doesn't really matter as much. We serve, in terms of interactivity, 200 tokens per second. People are fine [with that]. You don't need to go higher. The way people work has changed. We no longer look at the stream of thinking tokens. People run tasks in parallel and check in when the task is done." And if throughput is a concern, he notes engineers who sign in after 5 pm are getting closer to 800 tokens a second. However, it's worth noting that GLM hasn't replaced GPT or Claude entirely. The Chinese model is text only, so it isn't ideal for things like UI work. So instead, Revolut used a model router to direct vision queries to models like Gemini or GPT Luna while keeping code generation running on GLM. "Open source is now a…

articles.title: Wharfedale Denton 1S review: these compact little standmount speakers are all business
articles.content: Wharfedale Denton 1S: Two-minute review Wharfedale has been having a lovely old time with its range of ‘Heritage’ loudspeakers lately — revisiting, remixing and reworking some of its Greatest Hits. The new Denton 1S, though, is slightly different. It’s an update of a 1974 design that went all-out to present as modern and forward-thinking. And so this reinterpretation has a ‘modern retro’ vibe rather than the ‘antique’ feel of other Wharfedale ‘Heritage’ models. The curvy cabinet with its recessed front baffle, the mildly dramatic coaxial driver arrangement (which sees the tweeter positioned in throat of the mid/bass driver) and the handily compact dimensions are all attractive — and the option of a fairly deep blue as a finish doesn’t do any harm in this respect either. The numbers, both in terms of frequency response and of sensitivity, are encouraging too. And when they’re doing their thing, it’s immediately apparent that the Wharfedale Denton 1S are no mere pastiche — they are a profoundly competitive pair of loudspeakers on their own terms and yes, it's a good enough performance to make them some of the best stereo speakers on the market, right now. The sound is, ultimately, slightly small-scale — but it’s organised, confident, entertaining, loaded with detail and has real unity and singularity to the way it’s presented. Yes, $999 / £649 spent elsewhere on a small pair of passive standmount speakers will buy you something different in sonic terms, certainly, but it’s very debatable indeed as to whether it can buy you anything better . Wharfedale Denton 1S Review: Price and release date Launched May 31, 2026 List price of $999 / £649 / AU$1,699 The Wharfedale Denton 1S speakers are available now, and in the United Kingdom a pair will set you back £649. In the United States this solution costs $999, while in Australia the going rate is AU$1,699 or thereabouts. At this money, the just about cheaper Dali Sonik 1 might be their chief competition, at $900 / £449.99 / AU$849. And just to throw it out there, while many pricier options obviously exist, Cambridge Audio's Award-winning active L/R S can be yours for a little less, at $549 / £399 / AU$949. Something to consider, anyway. Wharfedale Denton 1S review: Features Coaxial tweeter / mid/bass driver ‘Brilliance’ switch Rear-facing bass reflex port Passive loudspeakers have purity of purpose and are, unless someone’s being bloodyminded, relatively simple devices. Their list of features is seldom exhaustive. It’s a sign of just how straightforward passive loudspeakers tend to be that the Denton 1S stands apart simply because of a small rocker switch on the rear of each cabinet. Unlike 1974’s original Denton 1, the Denton 1S features a truly coaxial driver arrangement. Here a 25mm soft-dome tweeter sits in the acoustic centre of a 165mm mid/bass driver made from polypropylene. Here, as with any coaxial driver, the idea is to offer superior time-alignment and driver integration. (Image credit: Future) With the forward-firing drivers bolstered by a rear-facing bass reflex port, Wharfedale is quoting a frequency response of 50Hz — 20kHz and sensitivity of 88dB — that second figure strongly suggests this speaker will be in no way tricky to drive. Of course, the orientation of the reflex port means that low frequency presence is likely to increase the closer to a rear surface the speaker is positioned — and that’s where the little rocker switches come in. It’s described as a ‘brilliance’ control, and its two positions are labelled ‘norm’ and ‘max’. The idea is that setting the switch to ‘max’ will give a 1.5dB boost to the 2 - 4kHz area, which should allow the upper frequencies to hold their own against the emboldened low end in the event that the reflex port is delivering a little too much of a good thing. Of course, it will take the listener roughly no time at all to establish whether or not they think the ‘max’ setting is a good idea or not. Features score: 5 / 5 Wharfedale Denton…

articles.title: Rumored RTX 5080 Super is delayed, while GPU prices are rocketing upwards
articles.content: Nvidia's RTX 5080 Super was rumored for January 2027, but fresh gossip suggests it's delayed Meanwhile, a new report on GPU prices observes a hefty price jump month-on-month Even lower-end GPUs are getting more costly at a faster pace, and the high-end is a nightmare — with no RTX 5080 Super riding to the rescue, it seems Nvidia's RTX 5080 Super has been strongly rumored of late, but there's now been a cloud of doubt cast over this potential addition to the Blackwell range — just as we've got more evidence of how dire the situation with GPU price hikes has recently become. VideoCardz spotted the latest from the rumor mill on the RTX 5080 Super, a graphics card that supposedly packs 24GB of video RAM, with Taiwanese tech site Benchlife reporting that Nvidia has delayed the GPU (assuming it's a real product in the first place, of course). We were told via other rumor peddlers that the 24GB spin on the RTX 5080 is theoretically planned for a January 2027 launch, but Benchlife asserts that the release date "remains unclear" and that Nvidia's board manufacturing partners have yet to receive any design details for the new model. Given that, according to Benchlife, the "probability is extremely high" that the RTX 5080 Super won't debut in January, considering that board makers were expecting to receive the mentioned design info back in October. This pushes the rumored GPU back at least a month, very probably more, and the idea of that is hardly surprising given the ongoing RAM crisis, which has been getting worse as 2026 rolls on. That affects video RAM, and it's the main driver of price spikes with graphics cards, which are starting to get out of hand, as evidenced by TechSpot's latest monthly report highlighting the current cost of GPUs across various regions. What TechSpot's monitoring data for October 2026 shows is that, as we already knew, high-end pricing has gone even further off the rails. The RTX 5080 is up 39% in the US and 40% in Germany month-on-month, for example, which is ludicrous, frankly — in the US it's now 120% over the MSRP at $2,200. The UK has seen an 8% hike over the past month, with this GPU now 40% over its MSRP in the country. Globally, it's 77% over Nvidia's recommended price on average. The RTX 5090 is even sillier, as we've seen for some time now , and stands at $9,400 in the US in October, some 370% over the already very expensive MSRP. If you can find the Blackwell flagship at all, that is. What's really worrying is that TechSpot's data shows lower-tier GPUs are now seeing some major price bumps. Want a humble RTX 5050 in the US? It's gone up 35% over the past month (an increase of over $100), so you'll now pay 68% over the MSRP. The RTX 5060 is creeping up in price in some European countries, too — it's up 7% in the UK and 13% in Germany. The RTX 5060 Ti 8GB has gone up more, with this GPU getting hiked by 10% in the UK, so it's now £440 compared to £350 back at the start of 2026. The 5060 Ti 8GB went up 6% in the US, too, so it's now 40% over the MSRP in total. There are hikes across the board for Nvidia, and AMD's Radeon GPUs are getting more expensive at an even faster rate currently. Again, lower-end graphics cards are suffering, such as RX 9060 XT models being up 10% on average month-on-month. The RX 9070 XT is also up 10% in the US since last month, and the increase in Canada has been a sickening 30% — in just one month. Analysis: a deteriorating situation for GPUs (Image credit: Future) What does all this tell us? That spiralling graphics card prices are very real, with some huge ongoing hikes for higher-end models — but this isn't just a top-end GPU problem any longer. The real concern is that lower-tier boards are also seeing more price inflation, and I don't think this is a problem that's going away. Indeed, based on the weighty amount of chatter about the memory crisis continuing to get worse in this final quarter of 2026 and into next year, there's every reason to believe that GPU prices…

articles.content: Elgato's Virtual Prompter doesn't need special hardware, and follows your voice as you read, keeping scripts near your webcam during presentations, recordings, and video calls. Elgato launches free Virtual Prompter for Mac and Windows On Tuesday, Elgato announced Virtual Prompter, a new feature in Elgato Studio that turns your computer screen into a teleprompter without external hardware requirements. There are two modes that users can utilize: docked or floating. Docked places the script in a strip along the top of your screen near your camera, perfect for maintaining eye contact while reading. Docked is free to use and has no time limits. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.content: The iPhone is already an excellent messaging and note taking tool, but going from idea to capture is a process that needs improvement. That's where SpeakON comes in, an AI hardware voice recorder. SpeakON is an AI communicator for your iPhone. Image source: SpeakON Your iPhone packs hundreds of tools into one pocketable product, but that utility comes with some level of friction. By the time you decide which app to open, select your input method, and start capturing an idea, that idea is likely lost. Skip all the hassle and use SpeakON , a MagSafe-attached voice recorder with built-in AI that analyzes your voice, organizes your captured notes, and outputs what's needed in the moment. Whether your iPhone is open to a specific app or locked in your pocket, SpeakON is ready to capture your voice with the press of a button. Continue Reading on AppleInsider

articles.title: iOS 27.3 Adds Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode to Safari
articles.content: With iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS Golden Gate 27.3, Apple is making major updates to Safari. The browser is getting a Vertical Tabs layout, which can be used instead of the standard horizontal tab bar. It's a change that pairs well with the iPhone Duo 's larger display, but it is available across iPhone, iPad , and Mac. Vertical Tabs are located on the left side of the display and use icons by default to save space, but there is an option to make the tab bar wider to show website titles as well. Vertical Tabs work with both Topics and Tab Groups to keep things organized. Topics are created when automatic Apple Intelligence tab sorting is turned on in iOS 27 . Pinning tabs by dragging, quickly swapping between Tab Groups, and other features also continue to work. The option to turn on Vertical Tabs is located in the Safari settings or in the View menu on Mac and ‌iPad‌. Apple is adding Adaptive Dark Mode for websites that don't have a dark mode design option by default. If you use ‌Dark Mode‌ and then browse to a website with a bright background color, Safari will offer an option to "Try" Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌. After tapping Try, Safari renders a ‌Dark Mode‌ version of the page that makes the background darker, changes text contrast, inverts logos and graphics, recolors vector artwork, lifts raised surfaces, and rebalances layered shadows. Each website will be adapted based on what's needed to make it readable, so not every tweak is applied to every site. You can opt to turn Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌ on for all sites or on a site-by-site basis after using it. If a site has a native dark mode or has a dark design already, Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌ won't activate. Developers can also add a tag that causes Safari to ignore Adaptive ‌Dark Mode‌ and show the website as the developer intended. Along with these visual changes, Apple is adding new Siri AI actions. ‌Siri‌ can take action on tabs and windows, sorting, moving, closing, and arranging in Tab Groups. ‌Siri‌ also has control over web history, and you can ask it to clear your history for a particular site and for a set time period, such as the last 10 days. ‌Siri‌ can already see what's on your screen, but soon, ‌Siri‌ will also be able to understand the full content of webpages, including non-active tabs and content not in view. You will be able to ask questions about information across websites, so if you have multiple tabs open when shopping for an item, ‌Siri‌ will be able to sort them by price or give you information on the product that you're looking at. Apple says the ‌Siri‌ awareness feature is coming, but it's not in the first beta. The changes to Safari are available for developers starting today in the latest betas. An Apple Intelligence-capable device is required for the ‌Siri‌ features. iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ 27.3 will launch this December after several rounds of beta testing to refine the new features. articles.title: Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds
articles.content: Stanford researchers tested 50 widely cited claims about LLMs against 20 current models. 44 percent of the findings are already "expired," and another 34 percent have weakened significantly. The average lifespan is just 15.7 months. Claims about what models can't do expire fastest. articles.title: Apple Fitness+ Gets Gym Strength Plans in iOS 27.3
articles.content: With iOS 27.3, Apple is adding a new Gym Strength workout to Apple Fitness+. It's a custom fitness option that generates a four-week plan based on a user's goals, experience, schedule, and equipment. People of all experience levels can use the feature, selecting workout days, areas of the body to focus on, and session length. Workouts have recommendations for exercises, reps, sets, and load, plus short video demonstrations from Apple Fitness+ trainers. Workouts each week are adapted based on progress from the prior week. Gym Strength is available on iPhone and iPad , and Apple Watch wearers will be able to see and log exercises, reps, and load, plus track workout metrics. Gym Strength is currently available in the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and watchOS 27.3 updates for Apple Fitness+ subscribers.
